scope: Synthetic verification of sealed-use accounting; no actual evaluation ledger created
implementation: Use the existing shared evidence-policy module for consumption, void classification and aggregate-only corpus reuse limits. Bind candidate, protocol, policy, assignment and selected-inventory checksums.
Hold an exclusive live execution lease throughout an attempt. Serialize ledger transitions and atomically replace flushed state before acknowledging the first-read callback.
A repeated callback is idempotent only through the same live attempt. A concurrent or restarted process cannot reopen an old attempt for evaluation.
Recover interrupted attempts through bookkeeping only: pre-read failures become void and retain candidate authorization; consumed attempts remain consumed.
Record disclosures immediately and retire the corpus even when a later failure occurs. Refuse further read acknowledgements after retirement. Aggregate-only completion preserves reuse.
Store only identities, state, result hashes and digested exception messages, without private names, paths, truth or predictions.
independent_review_repairs: The initial per-transition lock allowed a restarted runner to reuse a consumed attempt ID. A live execution lease and bookkeeping-only recovery close that gap.
The initial completion-only disclosure API missed disclosures followed by failure. Immediate durable retirement now persists across failure.
license_review: Apache-2.0 project code; Python standard library and existing shared policy only. No dependency or external asset added.
limitations: Outer checksum-bound run admission and the C# callback bridge remain unimplemented.
The outer runner must retain the live lease and must never treat bookkeeping recovery as permission to evaluate again.
This component does not validate candidate accuracy, grant approval or read corpus contents.
